title: Beyond geometric symmetry: Broadband linear relations in wave scattering
authors: Malte Röntgen, Sucui Luo, Xuelong Chen, Chenyu Zhang, Ruotao Ye, Tianshu Jiang, Wenlong Gao
abstract: The design and control of wave scattering, that is, of the reflection and transmission parameters of a device, is of ubiquitous importance. These parameters generally change with varying frequency, though certain \emph{frequency-independent} linear relations may exist between them. Reciprocity and geometric symmetry (reflections, rotations, etc.) are classic and well-known examples that are present in many devices and significantly ease their design. In this work, we go beyond these and introduce a new class of relations that cannot be induced by reciprocity or geometric symmetry. Choosing networks of waveguides as our workhorse, we discuss the conditions and consequences of such novel behaviour and showcase suitable example setups. We further experimentally test our predictions using coaxial cables and find excellent agreement in the broad frequency range between 0 and 1 GHz. Our work not only deepens the theoretical understanding of waveguide network dynamics, but also opens new avenues for applications in broadband signal processing, quantum information, and integrated photonics.
summary: This work introduces a method to find novel, broadband linear relations in wave scattering parameters that go beyond standard symmetries like reciprocity. By analyzing the effective Hamiltonian of waveguide networks, the authors show that the existence of a non-geometric symmetry guarantees such a linear relationship. This principle is demonstrated both theoretically and experimentally using coaxial cables.
main_problem: To identify and utilize novel, broadband, linear relations between wave scattering parameters that cannot be derived from conventional physical symmetries like reciprocity or geometric symmetry.
main_result: The existence of a non-geometric symmetry, characterized by a commuting operator Q, guarantees the existence of a broadband linear relation between scattering parameters, which was experimentally verified.
method: The analysis involves deriving an effective Hamiltonian for wave scattering in waveguide networks and imposing the condition that this Hamiltonian commutes with a symmetry operator Q across a broad frequency range.
model_or_system: The primary model is wave scattering in waveguide networks, implemented using coaxial cables, which are mathematically analogous to quantum graphs or RLC circuits. The dynamics are governed by an effective Hamiltonian H_s(k) derived via techniques like the Schur complement.
key_observables: Scattering parameters (reflection $r_i$ and transmission $t_{ij}$), which are measured over a broad frequency range (0 to 1 GHz).
important_parameters: Frequency (k), impedance mismatch ($\Gamma_L$), and the symmetry operator Q.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a broadband symmetry Q that commutes with the effective Hamiltonian H_s(k) for all relevant frequencies k.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate physical setups (coaxial cables, 3-port networks) and show the resulting scattering matrix relations for both symmetric and novel non-geometric cases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework by deriving the governing equations for wave propagation in complex networks, deriving the effective Hamiltonian H_s, establishing the link between symmetry in H_s and symmetry in the scattering matrix S_s, and finally presenting both theoretical derivations and experimental verification.
why_interesting: The methodology of finding hidden, broadband symmetries in the effective Hamiltonian to predict linear relations in the scattering matrix is a powerful tool for designing novel wave devices, bridging concepts from symmetry theory to applied electromagnetics and photonics.
